action.Q7A.003: In the loft by the measuring room. If you find it, I’ll thank you with a bow!
action.Q7A.x01: And is the first line any good?
action.Q7A.x02: The best! ‘Never fear, darling!’ Only without the second one it sounds as if I’m saying goodbye to someone at a station.
action.Q7A.x03: A perfectly ordinary thank-you will do.
action.Q7A.x04: I can’t do ordinary. But I’ll rehearse it!
action.Q7A.journal: Rudo lent his script to Mira to rest her drawings on. It should be in the technical archive loft.
action.Q7B.label: Take Rudo’s script
action.Q7B.001: ‘Never fear, darling!’ If only someone had told me that this morning, when I was only going to change a fuse.
action.Q7B.journal: I found Rudo’s script in the loft.
action.Q7C.label: Give the script back to Rudo
action.Q7C.001: Never fear, darling! Everything will turn out fine!
action.Q7C.003: Yes. And then I spend three whole acts proving I overdid it.
action.Q7C.004: Whatever you do, don’t cut that line.
action.Q7C.x01: Your script. It was in the loft under Mira’s drawings.
action.Q7C.x02: My script! All of it! Even the second act!
action.Q7C.x03: Rudo, give me that script right now. I’m locking it away until the premiere.
action.Q7C.x04: And what am I supposed to learn from?
action.Q7C.x05: I’ll copy it out for you. The original isn’t leaving this hall again.
action.Q7C.journal: Rudo has his script back. So there will be a premiere.
action.Q9A.001: It’s not according to the template. But here a weak signal isn’t thrown away; it’s just separated from the interference.
action.Q9A.002: You explained that precisely. May I show it to your teacher? Only if you agree.
action.Q9A.003: Yes. But he has to see my notes too, not just the clean schematic.
action.Q9A.x01: Hi. May I see what you’ve got under that template?
action.Q9A.x02: You may. Just please don’t laugh.
action.Q9A.x04: It goes a different way. Like when the queue in the canteen splits so the little ones don’t have to push in with the big ones.
action.Q9A.x05: Without the notes it’s just a line that looks like a mistake.
action.Q9A.x06: The notes go with it. I promise.
action.Q9A.journal: Jana lent me her schematic so I can show it to her teacher, Mr Dobrovič.
action.Q9B.label: Show Jana’s schematic to the teacher
action.Q9B.001: The wiring is different from the template. Why?
action.Q9B.002: Jana explains it here in her notes. It doesn’t discard the weak signal, it sends it down a second branch.
action.Q9B.003: That’s logical. Let her explain it at the exhibition in her own words. I’ll add my approval.
action.Q9B.004: That’s exactly what she was waiting for.
action.Q9B.x01: Excuse me, sir, have you got a moment? Jana drew this.
action.Q9B.x02: Everything for the exhibition has already been approved. But show me.
action.Q9B.x03: Comrade Headmistress will read every word, so Jana should write her explanation neatly.
action.Q9B.x04: Perhaps I’ve been waiting for a design like this myself. I just didn’t know it.
action.Q9B.journal: Mr Dobrovič added his approval for the exhibition to Jana’s schematic.
action.Q9C.label: Give Jana her approved schematic
action.Q9C.001: Can I really show it like this, my own way?
action.Q9C.002: Exactly like this. It’s your design and you know why it works.
action.Q9C.003: Then I’ll draw a second design too. Maybe one day I’ll have a whole notebook.
action.Q9C.004: I’d like to see that notebook one day.
action.Q9C.x01: Here’s your schematic. Your teacher has written his approval on it.
action.Q9C.x02: And what do I say if someone asks why it’s different from the template?
action.Q9C.x03: The same as you told me. The canteen queue and all.
action.Q9C.x04: It’ll be tidy. Every schematic with its notes.
action.Q9C.objective: If you like, find Jana in 1995, 2020 and 2035 too, and see what that support gave her.
action.Q9C.journal: If you like, find Jana in 1995, 2020 and 2035 too, and see what that support gave her.
action.Q10A.001: This is our class bell. Look, I shake it. Nothing.
action.Q10A.003: It isn’t. I’ve got it in my hanky. It’s just that the loop broke.
action.Q10A.004: At the end of the year I’m the one who rings it. Our teacher said I’ve got the steadiest hand.
action.Q10A.005: And who was supposed to fix it?
action.Q10A.006: Uncle Oto. But today Uncle Oto has four alarm clocks and not one free hand.
action.Q10A.007: Uncle Štefan in the yard has the leather. But children aren’t allowed in there.
action.Q10A.008: So I wrote him a slip. Uncle Štefan always says: ‘Slip, signature, materials.’
action.Q10A.009: ‘Slip. Please may I have one bit of leather for the bell. Zuzana, first year.’
action.Q10A.010: There’s a signature too. Without a signature, nothing.
action.Q10A.011: I’ll bring the leather and make the loop. Will you lend me the bell?
action.Q10A.012: I will. But be careful – it belongs to the class, not to me.
action.Q10A.013: And when you’ve fixed it, don’t ring it on the way. I’m supposed to ring it first.
action.Q10A.objective: Give Zuzana’s slip to Štefan in the workshop yard and collect a leather offcut.
action.Q10A.journal: Give Zuzana’s slip to Štefan in the workshop yard and collect a leather offcut.
action.Q10A.hint_step: Talk to Zuzana in the park about the bell that won’t ring.
action.Q10B.label: Hand Štefan Zuzana’s slip
action.Q10B.001: A slip. ‘Please may I have one bit of leather for the bell.’
action.Q10B.004: Slip, signature, materials. All in order. Nowhere does it say the signature has to be a grown-up’s.
action.Q10B.005: A narrow offcut from a strap. Just right for a loop. I’m keeping the slip.
action.Q10B.007: For the wall. I’ve never had such a nice slip here.
action.Q10B.008: And tell Zuzka I don’t need the little flower in the corner next time. But she’s welcome to draw it anyway.
action.Q10B.objective: Make a new loop for the bell from the leather offcut and hang the clapper on it.
action.Q10B.journal: Make a new loop for the bell from the leather offcut and hang the clapper on it.
action.Q10B.hint_step: Hand Zuzana’s slip to Štefan in the workshop yard.
action.Q10C.label: Hang the bell’s clapper on the new loop
action.Q10C.001: Loop through the eye, clapper in place, knot on the inside so it doesn’t rub.
action.Q10C.002: I’ll give it one careful tinkle. It rings. But Zuzana gets to ring it properly first.
action.Q10C.objective: Take the mended bell back to Zuzana in the park.
action.Q10C.journal: Take the mended bell back to Zuzana in the park.
action.Q10C.hint_step: In your bag, combine the leather offcut with the class bell.
action.Q10D.label: Give Zuzana the mended bell
action.Q10D.002: Try it. But gently – the loop is still new.
action.Q10D.003: Did you hear? That’s what the end of the year will sound like.
action.Q10D.004: Zuzka, now the whole park thinks the lesson is over.
action.Q10D.005: It isn’t the end yet. Twenty-four more days. That was a rehearsal.
action.Q10D.007: Thank you. You can have a go at hopscotch. But only up to four – grown-ups fall over after that.
action.Q10D.008: And whenever you hear the bell ring at the end of the year, wave. That’s the agreement.
action.Q10D.journal: Zuzana gave the whole park a trial ring. We agreed I’d wave at the end of the year.
action.Q10D.hint_step: Use the mended bell on Zuzana in the park.
entry.S31.001: Ivanka, 1962. My phone is as useless here as it was in 1995. I’m a bit more nervous.
look.S31.BOZO: Božo knows every train that stops here. My arrival isn’t in his timetable.
look.S31.ambient 1: A wooden luggage trolley. It squeaks, but it’ll outlive every one of my wheelie cases.
look.S31.ambient 2: A mechanical clock. No mains, no battery, and yet it keeps perfect time.
entry.S32.001: Here everyone asks everyone whose they are. In my case that would be a long answer.
look.S32.BERTA: Mrs Kovárová is sizing me up from the shoes upwards. Nothing escapes her.
look.S32.ambient 1: A well with a sturdy wooden cover and a bucket on a chain. Probably the most important spot on the green for gossip.
look.S32.ambient 2: A bicycle with mudguards and a bell. It travels in time too, but only forwards, and slowly.
look.S32.chalk_arrow: On a stone by the well there’s a chalk arrow and PARK underneath. Someone in Ivanka thinks of strangers too.
entry.S35.001: Here materials are issued only against a slip. If I needed more time, they’d have a form for that too.
look.S35.SKLAD: Štefan keeps records even of the bits I’d throw away.
look.S35.ambient 1: A sack of grain. Nothing here gets packed in plastic yet.
look.S35.ambient 2: A handcart. Its only engine is whoever pushes it.
entry.S36.001: Oto’s workshop. A covered lathe, the smell of oil, and alarm clocks ticking in every corner.
look.S36.OTO: Oto looks at everything first and only then says something. I can see why Gran liked working with him.
look.S36.ambient 1: A file with its handle worn to a shine. Oto holds it exactly where I hold mine.
look.S36.ambient 2: Every alarm clock shows a different time. Oto says that’s exactly the point.
entry.S34.001: The village hall before rehearsal. Here everyone plays someone else. I’m playing an ordinary visitor.
look.S34.LIDA: Lída is in charge of costumes, scenery and actors. All at once, and calmly.
look.S34.RUDO: Rudo is holding a dramatic pause. Apparently for twenty minutes now.
look.S34.ambient 1: A forest made of fabric has pleasantly predictable weather.
look.S34.ambient 2: A mayor’s hat. Rudo plays the mayor in it; the hat plays itself.
look.S34.clamp: The stage flat clamp has a loose screw, so the flat wobbles whenever anyone touches it. I’ve got the tools for that in my bag.
entry.S37.001: The park by the manor house. Someone is drawing on a bench, someone is playing hopscotch on the path. Nobody here is in a hurry.
look.S37.VERA60: Vera draws things so that the next person can repair them. At last, drawings I won’t curse.
look.S37.ZUZANA: Little Zuzana is playing hopscotch and counting the squares out loud. Beside her in the grass lies a bell that hasn’t rung yet.
look.S37.ZUZANA.variant1: Zuzana is drawing another hopscotch in chalk and counting the squares. Now and then she looks up to see whether I’m bringing the bell.
look.S37.ZUZANA.variant2: Zuzana plays hopscotch and rings the bell after every tenth jump. Vera doesn’t even look up any more.
look.S37.ambient 1: A bench in the shade. Sit down and do nothing? Within a minute I’d be checking the screws.
look.S37.ambient 2: The manor house above the park. It stood here long before ZVON, and it’ll stand long after.
look.S37.bird: A pigeon with a ring on its leg is sitting by an empty bowl. I’m not going to chase it; some feed would help more.
look.S37.hopscotch: A hopscotch in chalk on the path: eight squares and a half-circle at the top. The lines are straighter than in my drawings.
entry.S38.001: A hut, a pump and a bucket. Research into time starts out like gardening.
look.S38.ambient 1: There’s a pencil line on the bucket with ‘up to here’ next to it. The cheapest measuring instrument in Ivanka.
look.S38.ambient 2: The grass by the hut is trodden into a path. Someone comes here every day.
look.S38.door: A solid door with a new lock. Behind it is the measuring room.
look.S38.paper_boat: A paper boat is stuck in the grass by the channel. ZUZKA is written on its side in pencil. The captain stayed on the bank.
look.S38.pump: The pump’s leather cuff is leaking and the water isn’t circulating. It needs a new cuff.
exit.S38.to_S39.locked: Locked. Someone from the mechanical workshop probably has the key.
conn.S38.S39.locked: Locked. Someone from the mechanical workshop probably has the key.
entry.S39.001: Gran isn’t a gran yet. But she already has the look that switches off pointless questions.
look.S39.MIRA60: She’s thirteen years younger than me and still looks as if she’s about to send me off to wash my hands.
look.S39.ambient 1: The bulb gives off more heat than light. Gran would say: ‘Poor efficiency.’
look.S39.ambient 2: Mira crosses things out in her notebook, but she hasn’t torn out a single page. She’s keeping everything even now.
look.S39.plate: ORIGIN, VOICE, CONSENT, RETURN. Below: ‘Different data are not invalid data.’ The plate stays here; I need an imprint of it.
look.S39.plate.variant1: The plate has stayed where it was, without a scratch. I’m carrying its rule in the imprint.
exit.S39.to_S38.locked: Locked. Oto will only give me the key once the hand pump is repaired.
entry.S40.001: The loft. Where things are stored temporarily until the next century.
look.S40.ambient 1: An empty suitcase. In a loft where Mira keeps everything? I’ll check the lining, just in case.
look.S40.ambient 2: A thick beam with pencil marks and dates on it. Even the loft keeps a notebook here.
look.S40.box: A metal archive box with a lock. The kind you lock away things that mustn’t be lost.
look.S40.box.variant1: The copy and the registration form are locked in the box. One day Mira will move them into her collection.
look.S40.paper: Waxed paper. Made for taking an imprint of the plate.
look.S40.script: The cover says RUDO and NEVER FEAR, DARLING. At last, a piece of paper without a single equation.
entry.S33.001: A small post office with a counter. Here every piece of paper is weighed, stamped and recorded.
look.S33.POSTA: Alojz straightens the edge of a sheet of paper before he even looks at what’s on it.
look.S33.ambient 1: Stamps in sheets. Little pictures that decide whether a letter leaves.
look.S33.ambient 2: A wall calendar: June 1962. The only thing in Ivanka that tells me when I am without asking questions.
look.S33.carbon: Carbon paper for customers. With it I can make a second copy of the form.
entry.S57.001: Dúbravka, 1982. I won’t be born for another three years, and here I am already.
look.S57.ambient 1: Big letters about our shared future. I’ve just come from it, and I’m not telling anyone.
look.S57.ambient 2: A timetable on paper. Updated in pen.
entry.S58.001: My school, still almost new. It looks stricter than I remember it.
look.S58.ambient 1: A call for a work brigade, in big words. In short: on Saturday some planks need carrying.
look.S58.ambient 2: The Czechoslovak state emblem above the entrance. I know what year it is without my phone.
entry.S61.001: The same yard, only the lime is still a twig. On my photo from 2020 it isn’t here at all.
look.S61.ambient 1: A red pipe elbow. Years from now they may repaint it. The low wall and the rows of stones will stay.
look.S61.ambient 2: Its route decides whether one day there’ll be shade here or hot tarmac.
look.S61.niche: A dry cavity behind the service board: second row from the top, third stone from the left. Oto and Tóno both agree to the hiding place.
look.S61.niche.variant1: The jar with the bridge is in the cavity. I’ll leave it alone now and take it out in 2020.
look.S61.tree: The handcart’s rut runs right past the trunk. A guard would protect the young lime.
look.S61.tree.variant1: The guard is up; the cart will go round. Šimon still has to enter it in the plan.
conn.S61.S64.label: Window of the caretaker’s workshop, 1982
entry.S64.001: That boy is Tóno. A moment ago, as the caretaker, he was signing me into the visitors’ book, and now he’s carrying a school bag.
look.S64.OTO82: Oto is twenty years older. He still draws the lines on his drawings dead straight.
look.S64.TONO82: Twelve-year-old Tóno. Just as focused as the caretaker in 1995, only without the bunch of keys.
look.S64.ambient 1: The wooden model swallow is Tóno’s. One day he’ll copy it as a metal ornament for the same window.
look.S64.ambient 2: The plaster is still fresh. By 2020 it’ll be a shade greyer.
entry.S62.001: A small shop on the estate. The shop assistant knows every customer by name.
look.S62.RUZENA: Mrs Malá behind the counter. She’s straight-talking, but with a smile.
look.S62.ambient 1: Returnable bottles – you just bring them back to the counter. If only I could return like that, without a chronometer.
look.S62.ambient 2: It’s playing quietly. The shop assistant hears everything important anyway.
look.S62.jar: A clean preserving jar with a lid and a rubber seal. I’ll ask Mrs Malá behind the counter about it.
entry.S65.001: The part is small. The paperwork for issuing it has ambitions.
look.S65.MARTA82: Mrs Dobiášová has a stamp, but I don’t have to stand to attention in front of her.
look.S65.ambient 1: Every component here is recorded in pen, three times. In the future a computer will do it by itself. Five times.
look.S65.ambient 2: The clock above the counter keeps good time. It only seems to stop when you’re waiting to be served.
entry.S59.001: The school corridor. Silence, terrazzo, and the feeling that someone is writing me up in the class register.
look.S59.ambient 1: A notice about a Pioneers’ meeting. Big letters, date, time, all in good order.
look.S59.ambient 2: The floor I’ll be running down for the bell in thirteen years’ time.
entry.S63.001: The same cupboard as in 2020. It already looks as if it knows more than I do.
look.S63.ambient 1: One day a scuff will appear here, and I’ll be finding my way by it for decades.
look.S63.ambient 2: A globe with the borders of 1982. In a few years it’ll be out of date.
look.S63.workbench: Three connectors for the bridge, each a different shape. The board has no power; the tools are ready.
entry.S66.001: Future shade is stored here. For now, in the form of three planks.
look.S66.SIMON: Šimon knows how tall the lime will grow one day. I’ve seen the yard where it didn’t.
look.S66.ambient 1: A plan of the paths in the yard. Šimon can draw the tree guard and the cart’s new route on it.
look.S66.ambient 2: A spade. I’m not digging; I’m not planning a tunnel under the school.
entry.S60.001: The pupils’ technical exhibition. I’d better leave my phone in my pocket.
look.S60.DOBRO: Mr Dobrovič compares every piece of work with the template. Strictly, but with interest.
look.S60.JANA82: Jana is keeping her own design hidden for now, under the sheet with the template schematic.
look.S60.ambient 1: A template schematic labelled FOLLOW THE PROCEDURE. Jana looks at it as if she knows a better one.
look.S60.ambient 2: A school map of Czechoslovakia. Exactly as it should be in 1982.
look.S60.drawing: Jana has drawn her own improved design. She’s afraid to show it, because it isn’t the same as the template.
topic.BERTA.ambient 1.label: I’m here on a visit
topic.BERTA.ambient 1.001: I can see that. Nobody here has shoes like those.
topic.BERTA.ambient 1.003: That’s what everyone says who doesn’t want to dirty their Sunday best.
topic.BERTA.ambient 1.x01: And who might I be visiting here?
topic.BERTA.ambient 1.x02: That’s what you’re about to tell me. I’ve already ruled out half the village.
topic.BERTA.ambient 1.x04: I’ll have ruled them out by this evening.
topic.BERTA.ambient 2.label: Is it always this peaceful here?
topic.BERTA.ambient 2.001: Mostly, yes. Only that young Hrušková girl has her lights on again in the hut behind the park, in broad daylight.
topic.BERTA.ambient 2.002: That’ll be Gran. Well, a friend of mine.
topic.BERTA.ambient 2.x03: First you said ‘Gran’. My hearing is fine, young man.
topic.BERTA.extra 1.label: The little girl in the park
topic.BERTA.extra 1.001: Who’s the little girl playing hopscotch in the park?
topic.BERTA.extra 1.002: Zuzka. School in the morning, the park in the afternoon and the channel in the evening.
topic.BERTA.extra 1.003: She seems to know everything about Ivanka.
topic.BERTA.extra 1.004: She does. What Zuzka doesn’t know, I know. And what I don’t know hasn’t happened yet.
topic.BERTA.extra 1.005: And do you know anything about me yet?
topic.BERTA.extra 1.006: That you wear odd shoes. Zuzka will tell me the rest by this evening.
topic.BERTA.extra 2.label: Village news
topic.BERTA.extra 2.002: The neighbours opposite have a new radio. Now the whole street knows when the news is on and when it’s the brass band.
topic.BERTA.extra 2.003: And is that a good thing?
topic.BERTA.extra 2.004: For the news, yes. The brass band we could play ourselves.
topic.BERTA.extra 2.005: And in the hall they’re getting ready for a premiere. Rudo shouts so much at rehearsals you can hear him from here.
topic.BERTA.extra 2.006: Is there anything new at all that you don’t know yet?
topic.BERTA.extra 2.007: You, young man. That’s why I’m so curious.
topic.BOZO.ambient 1.label: Where can I find Mira?
topic.BOZO.ambient 1.001: Young Miss Hrušková? Measuring, behind the park. Oto in his workshop can tell you more.
topic.BOZO.ambient 1.002: Thank you. For now I’ll pretend to be an ordinary visitor.
topic.BOZO.ambient 1.x01: Ordinary visitors ask about the inn, not about Miss Hrušková. But good luck to you.
topic.BOZO.ambient 1.z01: And if you do get lost, little Zuzka is playing hopscotch in the park.
topic.BOZO.ambient 1.z03: She knows every corner of Ivanka. Better than I know the timetable, and I know that by heart.
topic.BOZO.ambient 2.label: The way back
topic.BOZO.ambient 2.001: Do you sell return tickets as well?
topic.BOZO.ambient 2.003: Even to a completely different year?
topic.BOZO.ambient 2.004: For that you’ll have to apply to the management. I only sell tickets to Bratislava.
topic.BOZO.ambient 2.x01: And where does the management sit?
topic.BOZO.ambient 2.x02: In Bratislava. So you’ll start with me anyway.
topic.BOZO.extra 1.label: Trains
topic.BOZO.extra 1.001: How many trains stop here a day?
topic.BOZO.extra 1.002: As many as are in the timetable. Not one more.
topic.BOZO.extra 1.004: Then it’s the same train, only later. It doesn’t turn into a different train.
topic.BOZO.extra 1.006: I don’t like uncertainty. A train that’s late at least knows where it’s going.
topic.BOZO.extra 2.label: Ivanka
topic.BOZO.extra 2.002: Just the right size. A church, a manor house with a park, a post office and a station. Everything a person needs.
topic.BOZO.extra 2.003: And the Little Danube just beyond the barns. When the wind’s off the water, you can smell it right up on the platform.
topic.BOZO.extra 2.004: And those aeroplanes over our heads?
topic.BOZO.extra 2.005: The airport’s right next door. The cows got used to it before the people did.
topic.BOZO.extra 2.007: I got used to it fastest. Aeroplanes have a timetable too.
topic.BOZO.extra 3.label: Advice for a traveller
topic.BOZO.extra 3.001: Have you any advice for someone who travels a lot?
topic.BOZO.extra 3.002: Where are you headed? That’s the first question. Without an answer I won’t even sell you advice.
topic.BOZO.extra 3.003: Honestly? To the year… to Mr Bielik’s workshop.
topic.BOZO.extra 3.004: Then you’re in luck. You walk there, and you don’t need a timetable.
topic.BOZO.extra 3.005: And if I didn’t know where?
topic.BOZO.extra 3.006: Then sit on a bench and wait until you do. The trains run anyway.
topic.DOBRO.ambient 1.label: What is the exhibition for?
topic.DOBRO.ambient 1.001: To show that the pupils have mastered the approved procedure.
topic.DOBRO.ambient 1.002: And when they’ve mastered it so well that they improve on it?
topic.DOBRO.ambient 1.003: Then they have to be able to explain it too.
